songInfo.title: (Sittin' On) The Dock of the Bay

scalesUsed.notes: G - A - B - C - D - E - F# - G
scalesUsed.application: Primary harmonic foundation for verse and chorus chord progressions
Vocal melody and simple guitar fills between chord changes
Bridge section melodic elements reflecting the relative minor tonality

mainProgression.description: Warm, soulful verse progression with the B7 adding a bluesy secondary dominant that resolves beautifully to C

sectionProgressions.description: The main four-chord cycle with a relaxed, gentle strumming pattern underlining the reflective lyrics

sectionProgressions.progression: G - E - G - E - G - A
sectionProgressions.romanNumerals: I - vi - I - vi - I - II
sectionProgressions.description: Back-and-forth movement between G and E creating a wistful, unresolved feeling that captures the song's contemplative mood
Standard I-V-IV movement providing harmonic stability and familiar resolution

harmonicFunction: G (I) - Tonic home chord establishing the warm, relaxed key center
B7 (III7) - Secondary dominant of vi (Em), adding soulful chromaticism
C (IV) - Subdominant providing gentle harmonic lift
A (II) - Major II chord adding gospel/soul color instead of the expected Am
E (vi as major) - The E major chord gives a bittersweet quality to the chorus
D (V) - Dominant chord in bridge for traditional resolution

techniques.name: Clean Strumming
techniques.description: Gentle, relaxed strumming pattern using open chord voicings with a warm, clean tone that captures the laid-back soul feel of the song

notes: G chord: 3-2-0-0-0-3 (standard open G voicing)
B7 chord: X-2-1-2-0-2 (open B7 voicing)
C chord: X-3-2-0-1-0 (standard open C voicing)
A chord: X-0-2-2-2-0 (standard open A voicing)
Use a relaxed down-up strumming pattern emphasizing beats 1 and 3
Keep the strumming hand loose for a gentle, unhurried feel
sequence: Strum down on beat 1 with a gentle, full strum across all strings
Light up-strum on the 'and' of beat 2 hitting the top 3-4 strings
Down-strum on beat 3 similar to beat 1
Light up-strum on the 'and' of beat 4 for rhythmic continuity
Let each chord ring for a full two beats before changing
tips: Don't grip the pick too tightly - a loose grip creates a warmer tone
Focus on smooth, even strumming rather than volume or speed
Let chords ring and overlap slightly during transitions for a flowing feel
Practice chord changes slowly and in isolation before playing the full progression

techniques.name: Smooth Chord Transitions
techniques.description: Moving between open chord voicings with minimal hand movement and maximum sustain, keeping the musical flow uninterrupted

notes: The G to B7 change shares the 2nd fret on the A string - use this as an anchor
The B7 to C change requires moving one finger at a time for smoothness
C to A involves lifting fingers from the C shape and placing the A barre
Keep common tones ringing through changes whenever possible
Practice each two-chord transition in isolation 20 times before combining
sequence: Play G chord for two full beats, begin moving to B7 on the last 8th note
Land on B7 cleanly, keeping the 2nd fret A string finger in place
Transition from B7 to C by shifting the index finger up one fret on the B string
Move from C to A by lifting the C shape and placing fingers for A
Repeat the cycle, focusing on eliminating any gaps between chord sounds
tips: Visualize the next chord shape while playing the current one
Use pivot fingers (fingers that stay on the same fret) to anchor transitions
Slow the tempo until every transition is perfectly clean, then speed up
Practice the B7 chord shape separately as it's the most challenging for beginners
details.progression: G - B7 - C - A (Verse), G - E (Chorus)

techniques.name: Fingerstyle Option
techniques.description: An alternative fingerpicking approach that can replace strumming for a more intimate, acoustic rendition of the song

notes: Thumb plays the bass note (root) of each chord on beats 1 and 3
Index and middle fingers play the higher strings on beats 2 and 4
Creates a gentle, rolling pattern that suits the contemplative mood
Bass notes: G string 6 fret 3, B7 string 5 fret 2, C string 5 fret 3, A string 5 open
sequence: Thumb strikes the bass note of the chord on beat 1
Index and middle fingers pluck the B and high E strings on beat 2
Thumb strikes the bass note again on beat 3
Index and middle fingers pluck again on beat 4
Maintain the chord shape throughout and let notes sustain
tips: Keep the picking hand relaxed and let fingers return naturally to position
Start with just thumb and one finger before adding more complexity
Let the bass notes ring through the higher plucked notes for fullness
This approach works especially well for the verse sections

sections.name: Intro
sections.description: Simple two-chord intro establishing the warm, relaxed feel of the song with gentle strumming over G and B7
notes: Set the tone with a gentle, unhurried strum
Let the G chord ring fully before moving to B7
Use a warm, clean tone with no effects
This intro sets the contemplative mood for the entire song

sections.name: Verse 1
sections.description: The verse introduces the main four-chord progression with a relaxed strumming pattern under the iconic vocal melody
notes: Each chord lasts approximately two beats (one half measure)
Keep the strumming gentle and even throughout
The B7 chord is the trickiest transition - practice it separately
Let the natural warmth of the open chords carry the harmony

sections.name: Chorus
sections.description: The chorus features the wistful G-E alternation for the 'sittinthe signature refrain, creating an emotionally resonant back-and-forth
sections.progression: G - E - G - E - G - A
notes: The E major chord adds a bittersweet quality - use the open E voicing
Emphasize the contrast between G (bright) and E (darker) moods
End the chorus pattern with the A chord resolving back to the verse
Slightly increase strumming intensity for the chorus emotional lift

sections.name: Verse 2
sections.description: Second verse repeats the same chord progression with identical strumming approach, perhaps with slight dynamic variation
notes: Maintain the same gentle feel as Verse 1
Transitions should feel completely natural by this point
Add very subtle dynamic variation to keep the performance alive
Focus on locking in with the vocal melody timing

sections.name: Bridge
sections.description: The bridge shifts to a G-D-C progression providing a moment of forward motion and harmonic contrast before returning to the verse
notes: The bridge uses familiar I-V-IV movement for stability
Slightly stronger strumming gives the bridge a sense of forward motion
The D chord provides dominant tension before resolving through C back to G
Keep the relaxed feel even as the harmonic rhythm picks up slightly

sections.name: Outro (Whistling)
sections.description: The famous whistling outro rides over the verse chord progression, with the guitar maintaining the gentle strumming pattern as the song fades out with ocean sound effects
notes: Maintain steady, gentle strumming as the whistling melody carries the outro
Gradually reduce volume and intensity for the fade-out
The chord progression loops the verse pattern until the fade
This is one of the most iconic outros in popular music history

alternatives: Hollow body electric (Gibson ES-335 or Epiphone Casino)
Any clean-toned guitar with warm pickups
guitar.pickup: Neck pickup for warm, round tone if using electric; natural acoustic resonance preferred

effects.reverb: Light spring reverb for subtle warmth and ambience
effects.other: No effects needed - simplicity is key to this song's tone

beginner.focus: Master the four open chord shapes and basic strumming pattern
steps: Learn the G, C, and A open chord shapes individually
Practice the B7 chord shape until it is comfortable and clean
Work on transitioning between each pair of chords in the verse progression
Strum the full G-B7-C-A progression at a slow tempo with a metronome

intermediate.focus: Develop smooth transitions and add the chorus and bridge sections
steps: Play the verse progression at full tempo (104 BPM) with clean transitions
Add the chorus G-E alternation with confident chord changes
Learn the bridge G-D-C section and practice song form transitions
Play through the entire song structure from intro to outro

advanced.focus: Add fingerpicking variation and dynamic expression for a polished performance
steps: Learn the fingerstyle picking pattern as an alternative to strumming
Add subtle dynamic variations between verses, chorus, and bridge
Practice transitioning between strumming and fingerpicking within the song
Perform the complete song with expression, dynamics, and confident timing

commonMistakes: Rushing through chord changes instead of letting each chord ring fully
Strumming too aggressively - this song requires a gentle, relaxed touch
Struggling with the B7 chord shape and producing muted or buzzing strings
Losing the laid-back feel by playing with too rigid or mechanical timing
practiceRoutine: Warm up with open chord shapes G, C, D, A, E, and B7 for 5 minutes
Practice the verse progression (G-B7-C-A) at 80 BPM with a metronome
Add the chorus section (G-E alternation) and practice the transition
Play the complete song form at gradually increasing tempos up to 104 BPM
focusAreas: Clean open chord voicings with no muted or buzzing strings
Smooth and gap-free transitions between chord shapes
Relaxed, gentle strumming feel appropriate to the soul genre
Song form awareness - knowing when each section changes
metronomeWork: Start at 70 BPM strumming each chord for four beats before changing
Increase to 85 BPM changing chords every two beats as in the song
Practice at 95 BPM with the full strumming pattern (down-up)
Reach target tempo of 104 BPM with confident, musical chord changes
